extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officials, and attorneys who practice before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures the USPTO uses to evaluate and discipline registered patent practitioners for professional misconduct (e.g., dishonored payments, neglect, dishonesty). Includes the specific regulatory provisions alleged to be violated, mitigating/aggravating considerations, and imposed sanctions and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§10.20-10.112) and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§11.101-11.901) apply to practitioner conduct; the Code applies to conduct prior to May 3, 2013, and the Rules apply on or after May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may rely on either the Code or the Rules depending on the dates of the conduct; practitioners are subject to these provisions while registered to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code proscribes engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing payments to the Office drawn on accounts containing insufficient funds resulting in dishonored payments is cited as conduct violating this prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code proscribes engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dishonored payments caused by lack of oversight were characterized as conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of an entrusted legal matter (37 C.F.R. §10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code proscribes neglect of an entrusted legal matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to timely pay fees to the Office for which clients had instructed or otherwise relied upon the practitioner to pay is treated as neglect of an entrusted legal matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. §11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules require reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to timely pay Office fees for which clients relied on the practitioner is a violation of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation under the Rules (37 C.F.R. §11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules proscribe engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order treats authorizing payments drawn on accounts without sufficient funds, causing dishonored payments, as falling within this proscription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct adversely reflecting on fitness under the Rules (37 C.F.R. §11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rules proscribe engaging in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dishonored payments and the attendant lack of oversight were cited as conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing fee for dishonored payments (37 C.F.R. §1.21(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: A $50 fee is required for processing each payment refused or charged back by a financial institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent represented that he paid the $50 processing fee for each of the eleven dishonored payments discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Director jurisdiction to impose discipline (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §11.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters concerning practitioners under these statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disciplinary action and approval of the settlement agreement are taken pursuant to these statutory and regulatory authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction types and probation/suspension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible sanctions include public reprimand, probation for a specified period (here, 36 months), and suspension for up to 36 months if probation terms or rules are violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director believes the practitioner failed to comply during probation, the OED Director issues an Order to Show Cause, serves it at the practitioner's address of record, grants 15 days to respond, and may forward the matter to the USPTO Director requesting immediate suspension for up to 36 months. The Agreement here imposed a public reprimand and 36-month probation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements for disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders are to be electronically published at the OED's FOIA Reading Room and a notice materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Public Reprimand and Probation' is to be published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the reading room URL and provides the exact language to be used (or materially consistent language) in the Official Gazette notice, including recitation of violating provisions and factual summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of suspension for practitioner credentials and access
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the USPTO will dissociate the practitioner's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates; the practitioner may not use or obtain USPTO customer numbers or PKI certificates until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These technical/access steps are immediate upon suspension and are a condition of suspension enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stay of suspension pending review or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any review or appeal of a suspension shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold the suspension in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension takes effect even if the practitioner seeks review or appeal; the procedure does not stay the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, in future complaints or proceedings involving the same or similar misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used (1) when addressing further complaints of similar misconduct, (2) in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor, and/or (3) to rebut statements made on the practitioner's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors affecting sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office considers mitigating factors (e.g., no prior disciplinary history) and aggravating factors (e.g., nature and amount of misconduct) when determining discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, the respondent's nearly 21-year registration with no prior disciplinary history was reflected as a mitigating consideration; respondent's acknowledgment of responsibility, payment of processing fees, and the total amount of dishonored payments ($7,825) also informed the agreed resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner responsibility for accounting and oversight of client-related payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must maintain adequate accounting and bookkeeping oversight to ensure payments to the Office on behalf of clients are honored; serious lapses may constitute misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged serious lapses in accounting/bookkeeping causing multiple dishonored payments; such lapses were treated as the factual basis for violations (neglect, lack of diligence, and dishonesty-related proscriptions).
